newsitem.title: CANADA: BC Sugar repeats rejection of partial bid.
newsitem.headline: BC Sugar repeats rejection of partial bid.

text.p: BC Sugar Refinery Ltd on Wednesday again urged shareholders to reject a partial C$15 a share bid from Balaclava Enterprises Ltd and repeated its endorsement of a competing C$14.75 a share offer for the entire company from Great Pacific Acquisition Inc.

Balaclava earlier said it was going ahead with its offer for 7.85 million shares in the sugar refiner and the bid is due to expire on May 30. Balaclava is a vehicle for Vancouver businessman Stuart Belkin while Great Pacific represents financier Jim Pattison.
In response, BC Sugar repeated its earlier advice to shareholders and said its financial advisors have concluded that the "effective value" of the Balaclava bid is only C$13.50 a share.

According to the advisors Nesbitt Burns, "the Great Pacific bid is financially superior to the Balaclava offer and is fair to the shareholders of BC Sugar, other than Great Pacific, from a financial point of view," BC Sugar said.
Furthermore the company said that Balaclava introduced on Wednesday "an entirely new condition" to its offer that the BC Sugar shareholder rights plan be eliminated.
BC Sugar said that "two other potential bidders have indicated that they are no longer participating in the auction process" for the company so only the two offers should be considered.
